sampling_model.design: Conditional on each fixed covariate stratum, \(Z\) is randomized with known \(\pi_z(x)=P(Z=z\mid X=x)\) and \(\min_{x,z}\{P(X=x),\pi_z(x)\}\ge\pi_*\); the observed count vector satisfies \(N_n\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}\{n,p_n(u)\}\).
sampling_model.units: The categorical support \(\mathcal J\), rational wage grid \(\mathcal Y\), rational quantile grid \(\mathcal T\), and assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\) are fixed while \(n\to\infty\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument \(Z\), received treatment \(D\), and selection indicator \(S\) are binary; wages are observed only when \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Carter's experiment comparison is used only on fixed positive-support multinomial strata with \(\min_j(p_0)_j\ge\kappa\). The causal bridge separately maintains randomized-instrument and stratum positivity plus aggregate \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\ge m_{*}>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The model-specific premises are \(p_n(0)\to p_0\) and \(\sup_{u\in C}\|\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\|_2\to0\) on every compact \(C\). The fixed pair \((p_0,B)\) determines \(\Sigma_0\). Every branch inequality is evaluated at \(p_0\): nonzero signs are frozen and zero-base cuts contribute the tangent normal \(a_j=B^{\prime}\alpha_j\). Thus \(\mathfrak G_0\) covers all directions without evaluating \(p_0+Bu\) as a law. Moving faces use \(c_{n,j}=\sqrt n\psi_j\{p_n(0)\}\), the displayed remainder, the compatibility subspace \(\mathcal K_0\), and the boundary charge \(\mathfrak b_0\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.4 proves that recession cones form a rational fan under connectedness and the Minkowski--Weyl condition.
Theorems 3.32 and 4.8 construct a compatible compactified polyhedral complex and compute its Hasse diagram combinatorially.
Corollary 4 gives an explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization error for Gaussian integration over a polytope.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a near-optimal affine detector for two compact convex composite hypotheses through a convex-concave saddle point.
Theorems 1--3 prove convergence of finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations to compact-parameter minimax expected-size confidence regions.
Theorem 1.3 gives a randomized \(O^*(n^3)\) relative-error algorithm for Gaussian volume of a convex set containing the unit ball in the membership-oracle model.
The paper gives convergence conditions for adaptive discretization of finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs with unbounded variables.
Theorem 1 bounds the Le Cam distance between a multinomial experiment and a matching Gaussian experiment when cell-probability ratios are bounded.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform coverage for calibrated projection under drifting moment inequalities, and Theorem 3.2 gives an optimization convergence rate on a compact rectangle.
The paper derives sharp marginal quantile-treatment-effect bounds under truncation by death.
Propositions 1--2 derive nonparametric bounds for average wage effects among always-employed compliers in Job Corps.

Under the complier-conditional weak-selection condition in Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1 gives sharp mean SLATE bounds for always-selected compliers, and Theorem 4.1 gives inference and joint asymptotic normality.

Theorem 1 proves minimum average Lebesgue volume for the inverted minimal-cardinality multinomial covering collections of Definition 1, and Proposition 1 selects a maximum-coverage tie-break among those minimizers.

Section 5 and Proposition 1 present sharp quantile-treatment-effect bounds for the always-employed stratum under random assignment and individual-level employment monotonicity, and Section 6.4 evaluates those bounds at multiple Job Corps wage quantiles.

body.tldr: The generic contribution remains effective compatibility density for globally honest semantic finite-label inference on an unbounded rational-semipolyhedral Gaussian fan. The rebuilt Job Corps bridge now forms a globally complete tangent arrangement by freezing nonzero branch signs at \(p_0\) and extending only zero-base directional cuts \(\alpha^{\prime}Bu\); it never treats the rank-positive vector \(p_0+Bu\) as a probability law. The finite moving-slack vector, compatibility subspace, Gaussian boundary charge, four-label primal rule, atomic dual, and contact rule are all exhibited. Selection monotonicity is imposed only among compliers, as in Dong and Heiler. Conditional on the open effective-density theorem, CertGluePFL and the transfer theorems deliver replayable simultaneous labels for the same-law coordinatewise Job Corps quantile endpoints.

project_justification.gap: Existing geometry makes recession incidences compatible, existing numerical analysis encloses individual Gaussian-polytope integrals, and existing decision theory treats compact parameter classes. Existing Job Corps work includes average and multiple-quantile wage-effect bounds for always-employed survivors under assignment and average bounds for always-employed compliers under noncompliance. The missing theorem is a simultaneous rule-level approximation over the entire unbounded incidence diagram with one computable weighted modulus, followed by a complete primal-dual stopping recurrence and moving-face multinomial transfer for coordinatewise sharp always-selected-complier quantile-effect labels.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification assertions create discontinuous loss and coverage constraints at intersecting faces, while least-favorable means and dual mass can escape along several incident cones. This structure is neither a compact convex hypothesis test nor a routine finite-dimensional semi-infinite program.
project_justification.fill: Nested covariance-orthogonal averaging, the explicit homogeneous recession refinement, semantic projection, weighted path accounting, repair, and atomic dual enumeration form the generic certificate program. The causal bridge uses the full complier-restricted latent fiber and a globally completed tangent fan built from active cuts at \(p_0\). The moving-offset system and four-label benchmark now have explicit finite constructions and receipts.

body.related_work: Burgos Gil and Sombra (2011, Theorem 3.4) prove qualitative common-face compatibility of recession cones by lifting a polygonal path through a Minkowski--Weyl support; Kastner, Shaw, and Winz (2025, Theorems 3.32 and 4.8) make the compactified incidence diagram combinatorial. Jones and Peet (2018, Corollary 4) propagate explicit smoothing, truncation, and gridding errors for one Gaussian-polytope integral, while Cousins and Vempala (2018, Theorem 1.3) provide randomized \(O^*(n^3)\) relative-error Gaussian-volume computation for convex sets containing the unit ball. Goldenshluger, Juditsky, and Nemirovski (2015, Theorem 2.1), Armstrong and Kolesár (2021, Sections 2.3 and 2.5), and Schafer and Stark (2009, Theorems 1--3) establish computable optimal or near-optimal Gaussian procedures on compact convex or compact parameter classes. Jungen, Djelassi, and Mitsos (2022) show why unbounded semi-infinite discretization needs explicit convergence hypotheses. Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) supplies parameter-independent recursive multinomial--Gaussian comparison kernels under positive cells; it is not cited for the model-specific uniform triangular-array affine expansion maintained here. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Theorem 3.1) show how drifting active inequalities affect uniform coverage. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2021, Definition 1 and Theorem 1) give minimum-average-volume exact multinomial confidence sets; this is an informed finite-sample benchmark rather than a claimed extension target. Imai (2008) gives sharp survivor marginal quantile bounds. Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013, Section 5, Proposition 1, and Section 6.4) give Job Corps average and multiple-quantile wage-effect bounds for the always-employed survivor target under assignment. Chen and Flores (2015, Propositions 1--2) treat Job Corps always-employed complier means under noncompliance. Dong and Heiler (2026, Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1, and Theorem 4.1) impose complier-conditional weak selection monotonicity, establish sharp mean SLATE bounds for always-selected compliers, and give inference with joint asymptotic normality. The causal contribution here instead targets the always-selected-complier quantile-effect vector on a finite quantile grid under noncompliance and covariate-directional selection, defines coordinatewise sharp endpoints through same-law fiber optimizations, and supplies simultaneous semantic-label honesty with replayable minimax certification. None of these comparators contains the unbounded recession-compatible rule-density theorem or the moving-face Gaussian-to-multinomial certification kernel.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The strongest rigorous four-label enclosure remains \(0.361100\le M_{\mathfrak G_4,0.05}(2)\le0.813799\), of width \(0.452699\), although its rule and atomic dual are now fully defined. Effective simultaneous incidence density, complete CertGluePFL recurrences, the milliscale certificate, and the diagonal common-rule moving-offset proof remain open. The global Job Corps object is a tangent completion: its causal interpretation is asserted through the compact-away-from-boundary transfer statement, not by pretending \(p_0+Bu\) is lawful for all \(u\). The joint quantile-effect identified set is only contained in the product of coordinatewise intervals.
body.honest_scope: The generic unbounded-fan kernel and headline statements are unchanged. The redundant recession-fan assumption has been removed because the homogeneous arrangement constructs the fan. The Job Corps Gaussian object is now a globally completed tangent experiment, with a proved-as-obligation cover sanity reduction and an exhibited separated point. Selection monotonicity is complier-conditional; noncomplier selection responses remain unrestricted. Moving transfer is conditional on effective compatibility density and on the displayed finite slack expansion. The four-label numerical enclosure is attached to explicit primal, dual, and contact objects; the milliscale gap remains open.
